_what: What the tool that adds a source of tools (do-work/add-tool-source.mjs) reads and says. A source is one address; what kind of source it is (`folder`, `repo` or `remote-mcp`) is learned once, here, and kept with how it was learned: the person never types a kind. The order is fixed by the owner's decision case source:a2VlcC1vbmx5LWJyaWFucy1kYXRhLWFuZC13aXBlLXRoZS1ib3hlcy0yMDI2LTExLTE2 (tool sources of any kind): first the address's own syntax (`prefixes`, then `repo_hosts`), then, only for a bare https address, ONE probe: an MCP `initialize`, else a git `info/refs`, else a refusal naming both. The engine never probes and never guesses (trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools/sources.rs `merge`).

_why.timeout_ms: 10 s for each request: a server that is a server answers a first request well inside it, and the probe makes at most four. A reasoned bound, not a measured one.
_why.max_bytes: 64 KiB of an answer is read: an MCP initialize answer and a git ref advertisement's first lines fit with room, and no more is needed to tell which one it is. A reasoned bound, not a measured one.
_why.max_redirects: Three redirects are followed, each to an https address, so an address that moved once or twice still answers and none loops. A reasoned bound, not a measured one.

repo_hosts_what: The hosts whose https address of the form host/owner/repo is a git repository by its syntax alone, and the address each serves a commit's archive at (`{repository}`, `{commit}`), with the hosts that archive is read from. A git server not listed here is refused with its host named: its archive address is not known.

row._what: A pending request, never a list of sources: one question for the person per address, at `prefix` + the label, kept until the person approves or declines it (the screen that asks them deletes it). The engine's own list of the account's sources (tools:sources) is the one list; tools:add-source is the person's act, never the AI's.

words.no_address: Give the address of the source: a folder's path, a git repository's https address or a remote MCP server's https address.
words.bad_address: That is not an address I can add: give a path that starts with / or ~/, or an https address.
words.bad_label: A label is letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, and starts with a letter or digit.
words.taken: A source called {label} is already waiting or added. Pick another label, or remove that one first.
words.no_ssh: I do not add ssh or git@ addresses. Give the repository's https address.
words.no_http: A plain http address is added only when you say it is a server of your own: write it as mcp+http://host:port/path.
words.private_named: A server at {host} is a private address: it is reached only because you named it with mcp+http://.
words.credentials_in_address: An address with a user name or password in it is not added. A server that needs a sign-in asks for one when it is first used.
words.unknown_archive: {host} is a git server, but I do not know where it serves a commit's archive. I can add repositories from {known}.
words.not_a_repository: {address} names no repository: a repository's address is host/owner/name.
words.ambiguous: {address} answers as an MCP server and as a git repository. Say which it is: mcp+{address} or git+{address}.
words.neither: {address} did not answer as an MCP server ({mcp}) or as a git repository ({git}). If you know which it is, write mcp+{address} or git+{address}; a server of your own at a private address is written mcp+http://host:port/path.
words.no_commit: {address} answered as a git repository but named no commit to start from. An empty repository has nothing to add.
words.added: {label} is ready to add as a {kind} source ({learned}). Nothing is added until you approve it: it is your act, at the engine's tools:add-source. It starts with an empty grant: none of its tools may use your records, credentials or hosts until you say so.
words.folder_note: A folder holds one folder of tools inside it called tools.
words.credential_only_for_servers: A credential belongs to a remote MCP server; a folder or a repository takes none.
words.one_credential: Give either a credential (a vault name) or a connection, not both.
words.bad_credential: A credential is the name of a secret in your vault; a connection is {connection_id: service_connection:<service>, field_id}.

credential._what: A server that asks for a sign-in is read with the bearer the person's connect tool keeps in their vault (tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key): the source names that vault name and the engine sends it only to that server's host (trillion-rust remote_mcp.rs). A service connection's field is kept under `held_prefix` + the hex of its connection id + `field_separator` + the hex of its field id (trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools.rs held_name), so the tool can name it from the connection and field. The name only: no value is read or written here.
